We have noticed a potentially significant difference concerning patient care and the measurement results which are provided in the TAVI PLANNING-tool, depending on which version that was actual during the time of measurement. The final TAVI-unit dimension is normally 2mm bigger than the results which are provided from splice-contour measurement in the first phase of TAVI-planning. It should be noted that in these two measurements, the measurement object is exactly the same and measurement points are set on the same. Attached two patient examples. They were never sent, they are anonymizing and sending the examples to me as-of-writing. We have used the results of unit size to make the decision on choice of valve. If this measurement is too big, this could potentially lead to a choice of wrong valve design and size which in turn can lead to aplication. This matter was brought to our attention recently since the analysis of a few patient with 3Mensio software, which results were regularly a couple of mm smaller than the measurements form our tool for choice of size of units.
